rules.sentence: While rare, with less than 1% of Alzheimer disease cases, familial Alzheimer disease is believed to be caused by genetic mutations in amyloid precursor protein, presenilin-1, and presenilin-2.
About half of the individuals with these mutations develop Alzheimer disease before age 60.
The condition causes cognitive deficits like memory impairment, language disturbance, disorientation, and even noncognitive issues like personality changes.
It makes up less than 1% of all Alzheimer disease cases and has a neuropathogenesis similar to familial Alzheimer disease.
